Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 75, verse 16–25:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾. Whenever the revelation came down to him, he would move his tongue and lips before Jibril had finished reciting the revelation, fearing that he would not retain it. So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse." Its meaning: do not move your tongue with the Qur'an in order to hasten its acquisition. ﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.﴾ Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, to gather it and bring it together in your breast. ﴿So when We have recited it﴾, that is, when We have gathered it, ﴿then follow its recitation﴾, that is, its collection. The exegetes said: meaning, recite it when Jibril has finished reciting it. Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿then follow its recitation﴾, that is, act upon it. Qatadah said: follow its lawful and its unlawful. ﴿Then indeed upon Us is its explanation﴾. Concerning this there are four opinions.

The first: We will explain it through your tongue, so that you recite it as Jibril taught you. When Jibril came to him, he would lower his head, and when he had gone, he would recite it as Allah had promised him. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: indeed it is upon Us to recompense for it on the Day of Resurrection with what it contains of promise and threat. This was said by al-Hasan.

The third: indeed it is upon Us to explain what it contains of rulings, the lawful and the unlawful. This was said by Qatadah.

The fourth: it is upon Us to send it down as an Arabic Qur'an, in which there is clarification for people. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Nay﴾. 'Ata' said: that is, Abu Jahl does not believe in the Qur'an or its explanation. Ibn Jarir said: the meaning is: the matter is not as you say, that you will not be resurrected; rather, your love of the immediate life has led you to say that.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Rather, you love the immediate life﴾. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited "Rather, they love the immediate life and leave behind" with the ya' in both places. The rest recited with the ta' in both places. The intended referents are the disbelievers of Makkah, who love it and work for it, ﴿and leave behind the Hereafter﴾, that is, they abandon work for it, preferring the world over it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Faces on that Day will be radiant﴾, that is, shining with bliss, ﴿looking at their Lord﴾. Ata' narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "Looking at Allah." Al-Hasan said: it is fitting that they should be radiant while looking at the Creator. This is the view of 'Ikrimah. The vision of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is true, without doubt, and the hadiths concerning it are sound; I have mentioned a body of them in "al-Mughni" and "al-Hada'iq".

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And faces on that Day will be gloomy﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, frowning and scowling.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Expecting﴾. Al-Farra' said: that is, knowing. And "al-Faqirah" is the calamity. Ibn Qutaybah said: it derives from the vertebra of the spine, as if it breaks it; it is said, "faqartu al-rajul" when you break his vertebra, just as one says "ra'stuhu" when you strike his head and "battanahu" when you strike his belly. Ibn Zayd said: al-Faqirah is entry into the Fire. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: it is being veiled from their Lord, so that they do not look at Him.
